learnings: Each process has its own interpreter and GIL, so CPU-bound work scales across cores.
Arguments and results are pickled between processes – small tasks can be slower in parallel than sequentially.
`shared_memory` shares one buffer by name instead of copying it; always `close()` and `unlink()` it.
pitfalls: Forgetting `unlink()` leaks the OS shared-memory block until reboot – a test now proves it is released.
